title: add zone reshuffle controller and egress policy templates
author: Sana Patel
release_notes: Introduce a zone-reshuffle controller and a set of templated egress security-group/route/privatelink policies to improve controlplane subnet failover and DNS mirroring. Backwards-compatible; opt-in via installer flag 'enable_zone_reshuffle'.
description: Context: Customers running private control planes across 3+ AZs have hit cases where long-lived controlplane subnets become skewed (overcommitted in one AZ) after incremental scaling and manual decommissions. This causes egress hotspots and occasional Route53 propagation inconsistencies during failovers. This PR introduces a "zone-reshuffle" controller plus a small set of templated egress artifacts to make staged AZ rebalancing and DNS mirroring safer and automatable. Motivation: reduce manual subnet shuffling during upgrades and make egress routing deterministic during staged controlplane failovers. Main changes: 1) Terraform module: new controller CRD role and service account resources to allow the reshuffle controller to observe subnet annotations and create temporary ENIs/route targets needed for controlled handoffs. 2) Helm chart: added deployment, leader-elect config, and a new values flag (enableZoneReshuffle) with schema validation and docs. 3) Installer scripts: idempotent migration that adds required tags/annotations to existing subnets, and a dry-run mode for customers to validate reshuffle plans. 4) Egress templates: AZ-scoped SG + route templates for pre-warming egress targets and conditional Privatelink policies for graceful cutover. 5) Tests: lightweight integration e2e to validate a 3-step reshuffle plan and DNS mirroring TTL adjustments. Checklist: - [x] Terraform module changes implemented with backward-compatible defaults - [x] Helm values and schema updated - [x] Installer migration script with dry-run mode - [x] Unit tests for template rendering - [x] Integration e2e validating routing and DNS mirroring - [x] Docs: operator guide and rollback steps Why this is low-risk: features are opt-in via helm flag enableZoneReshuffle=false by default. Migration script only adds non-destructive tags/annotations unless run with --apply. Security considerations: controller RBAC limited to read on subnets and write on ephemeral ENI/route objects scoped to the controlplane namespace. Design notes: the reshuffle controller implements a staged plan: 1) analyze AZ utilization, 2) plan minimal subnet moves, 3) pre-create egress ENIs and SG bindings in target AZs, 4) switch routes and update DNS mirror entries, 5) retire old ephemeral artifacts after health confirmation. Commit summary: - 1c2d8a9: add terraform module scaffolding and RBAC rules - 4b7f3e1: helm chart deployment and values.schema.json - a9d5c2b: implement installer migration script with dry-run - b2f45ab: egress AZ template and example manifests - e6f88c3: add integration test harness and fixtures Changed areas (high level): - terraform/modules/controlplane/subnet-controller adds aws_iam_role, aws_iam_role_policy, and template_file for controller config - helm/controlplane adds deployment.yaml, rbac.yaml, and new values entry with validation - installer/upgrade adds migration script and operator docs - installer/templates adds az-egress-template.yaml and sample policies - tests/integration adds reshuffle e2e that runs in CI as optional stage Review conversation snapshot: - Luca Moreno (review): "Controller looks generally good; can we reduce the frequency of AZ utilization polling?" - Sana Patel (author): "Lowered default polling to 15m and made it configurable via values.pollIntervalMinutes. Also added backoff jitter to avoid thundering herd during large fleets." - Jared Kim (review): "Small nit: split the terraform IAM policy into reusable statements and document the least privilege rationale." - Sana Patel: "Split the policy into three statements and added a short doc blurb in terraform/README.md." - Priya Anand (approver): "Verified migration script in a staging cluster. Works as expected with dry-run and apply. Approving to merge after CI green." CI details: - Unit: pass - Static lint (terraform fmt, tflint, helm lint): pass - Integration (optional): pass on staged runner - Security scan: pass (no secrets, policies follow least-privilege) Merge outcome: squash and merge performed by Priya Anand; commit message combines the feature summary and migration steps. Post-merge actions: - Publish release note entry under private-installer v0.18.0 - Add opt-in toggle to customer upgrade playbook - Schedule a canary rollout with two pilot customers next week Known limitations and follow-ups (tracked ENG-2190): - Current heuristic may prefer reshuffles that increase cross-AZ traffic; follow-up work will integrate cost/latency signals. - Add metric for reshuffle_attempts and reshuffle_success_rate to Redwood Console dashboards. Troubleshooting and rollback: installer/docs/zone-reshuffle.md contains step-by-step rollback including how to reassign tags to rehydrate original routing and how to remove ephemeral egress artifacts. Related PRs and context: ties to earlier subnet-recon PRs where we added annotation schemas; this is intentionally independent but compatible with those schemas.
